notes:
POC objective: validate Dedicated capacity can meet sustained throughput and tight latency SLOs for multi-tenant retail workloads. Representative traffic: short chat (20-50 tokens), assisted search rerank (avg 120 tokens per query with 5 candidates), personalization embedding generation (single-req batch size 64).

Key technical constraints / asks:
- P95 target: <=120ms for 32-token chat responses (streaming enabled).
- Throughput target: steady-state 250 requests/sec for chat endpoints; peak bursts to 400 rps for 30s windows.
- Token-cost sensitivity: want unit-cost targets for 2x growth scenario.
- Must support VPC peering + customer-managed KMS; SSO via Okta (SAML).

POC setup notes: Diego to provision 4-GPU pool with dedicated KV cache on worker nodes. Will run 3-phase tests: ramp, 72h soak, failure/rollback scenarios. Use quantized model variant for cost guardrails; compare to fp16 baseline.

Quote from CTO on 2026-02-20 call: "If you can't guarantee the tail latency, we can't move to reserved capacity — customer experience is unforgiving."

Stubs/refs: drive plan, ticket IDs above, Fireflies transcripts for discovery and kickoff.
poc_plan: Phase 1 (baseline): run smoke + 1h ramp to validate config and warm caches
Phase 2 (load): repeated 6h runs at target throughput to measure steady-state metrics
Phase 3 (soak): 72h continuous run with realistic traffic mix; monitor memory, KV hit rates, CPU/GPU saturation
Phase 4 (failure): simulate node OOM and degraded disk, validate graceful fallback to model variant and routing policies
Phase 5 (report): compile perf vs cost delta, recommended reserved GPU count, quantization tradeoffs
pricing_and_sla_notes: Negotiation points: committed GPU count and guaranteed throughput windows, financial credits for missed SLOs, support response time for P1 incidents. Highline is asking for explicit fallback model mapping and cost caps for unexpected token surges.
